chunks: Muhammad narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For everything there is a face, and the face of your religion is the Salat; so let not one of you disgrace the face of his religion. And for everything there is a nose (or pride), and the nose of the Salat is the Takbir.'

key_terms.أَنْفٌ: Nose (metaphor for pride, distinguishing feature, or essence)
key_terms.وَجْهٌ: Face (metaphor for excellence, dignity, or visible aspect)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Salat as the 'face' of religion and Takbir as its 'nose' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of the 'face' (wajh) to signify that prayer is the visible dignity and public manifestation of Islam, while the 'nose' (anf) represents its distinguishing pride and essential entry point. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on both the external correctness (adab) and internal spiritual presence (khushu) of the believer, warning that negligence in the ritual's form disgraces the faith itself. The identification of Takbir as the 'nose' highlights its role as the definitive marker that distinguishes the Islamic prayer from other acts of worship.
